executiveSummary: The support team's Q3 update to the VP of Customer Experience: waits halved after the triage bot launched, and the team asks to fund its second phase rather than hire.

slides.slideTitle: Support in Q3: shorter waits, and what's next
slides.subtitle: Customer Experience staff meeting · October 9
slides.speakerNotes: - Thanks, everyone. This is the Q3 support update.

slides.slideTitle: Customers told us waiting was the worst part
keyBullets: Top complaint in all four 2025 surveys
slides.speakerNotes:
- Every survey last year said the same thing: the wait was the problem, more than the answers.
- Forty-one percent of our detractors named it.

slides.slideTitle: We moved the whole team to the third floor in June
slides.speakerNotes: - The move went well. Everyone is together now, and the queue board is on the wall where people can see it.

slides.slideTitle: We hired six agents this quarter
keyBullets: All six finished training by September
slides.speakerNotes: - We brought on six new agents, and all of them are taking tickets now.

slides.slideTitle: The new training program cut ramp time to three weeks
keyBullets: Shadowing in week one, live tickets by week two
Every new agent has a buddy
slides.speakerNotes:
- We rebuilt onboarding this year. New agents shadow for a week and take live tickets in week two.
- Ramp time went from six weeks to three.

slides.slideTitle: Engagement rose to 78 in the August pulse survey
keyBullets: 78 in August, up from 64 in March
slides.speakerNotes: - The team is happier. The August pulse came in at seventy-eight, up fourteen points.

slides.slideTitle: On-call is fairer now that it rotates weekly
keyBullets: No one on call two weeks running
slides.speakerNotes: - We changed on-call to a weekly rotation, so nobody gets stuck with it.

slides.slideTitle: Headcount alone would not have gotten us here
slides.speakerNotes: - I want to be clear that it wasn't only the hiring.

slides.slideTitle: Agents say they have time for the hard tickets again
keyBullets: “I finally get to finish a hard case without five more piling up.”
slides.speakerNotes: - Priya said this in our retro, and I heard it from several people.

slides.slideTitle: The bot halved our waits: fund its second phase, not more agents
slides.subtitle: Decision needed by October 30
keyBullets: The same gain from hiring: about nine agents, $430,000 a year
slides.speakerNotes:
- So the ask is to fund the bot's second phase at a hundred and forty thousand, and hold headcount where it is.
- Getting the same result by hiring would take about nine agents.
